Built: reader-only packed count slots with main's two-argument closure/method ABI; optional and rest binding needs no count.
Commits: implementation 89c8e81e; benchmark baseline 71d7e491; current main integration 48c05d091f0a43c31cbe051b1d6578d99eeedf19; all post-merge checks passed.
Commands and outputs: final release stage 1 parse, best of five wall time against 71d7e491: main 11.504 ms, integrated revision 12.113 ms; 10,523 nodes each. Before integration: 10.351/9.557 ms and byte-identical C/binaries. After integration: byte-identical C/binaries to current main.
Mutants: nine killed, including an unwanted nonreader count caught by TestNoReaderCallingConvention's pinned emitted-C count-slot check.
Not covered: instructions and cycles are unavailable on this box: perf_event_open returns ENOENT for both hardware events. No complete ./... test gate; original unsupported spread/rest forms remain unsupported.

Calling convention

The universal third argument has been removed from closure.code and adamic_method, including array sort and collection iterator runtime calls. The original two-argument calling convention remains. The hidden count is a designated numeric slot in the existing packed argument buffer, present only if the resolved function type has an actual reader candidate. Optional slots are padded by the caller; rest tails are collected into separately reserved slots. Neither binding requires a callee count. Merely reserving stable IR offsets emits no instructions.

Reader facts are distinct from uniform virtual signatures: sharing a native signature with a reader never turns an implementation into a reader candidate. Virtual implementations still share their slot's typed C signature when that slot has a reader. Named-function value adapters get a hidden local only when their forwarded function reads the count. Callback checker types are recorded so library calls select their own candidate set, rather than inheriting unrelated readers. Known empty types stay empty; an unresolved closure with unknown targets conservatively includes the program's functions, while a bounded closure uses its targets.

The no-reader fixture covers optional values, explicit undefined, defaults, numeric rest arrays, rest spreads and an interface method. Its C has no hidden count slots or count local. The unrelated-type fixture contains a reader and a string-returning nonreader function value; exactly the reader-compatible call has a count slot. Both fixtures join the Node oracle for .a and temporary .ts sources.

Retain changes

Observed: weak_parent retains/releases were 255/304 on 2ac11b57, now 253/302, matching 71d7e491. typeof_dispatch was 7/17, now 6/16, matching 71d7e491. The complete recorded-count gate passed before merging newer main.

Cause: fitCallArguments converted fixed arguments before ownership planning. In weak_parent this materialized two owned Weak values; in typeof_dispatch it materialized one owned Union value. Those values added balanced retain/release pairs. The numeric count did not retain anything. Fixed fitting is now left to the existing native call boundary after planning, as on main. Only rest-tail element fitting remains in lowering. No other pre-existing fixture count row changed against 71d7e491; changes in the new unit fixtures reflect caller-side rest arrays.

Release measurement

Both Go compiler binaries were built with go build -buildvcs=false. Adamic build uses the default release flags (-O2, no sanitizer or runtime counting). Both compile the same canonical /workspace/adamic/stage1/typescript/parser/main.ts entry. Each parser was called with --manifest /tmp/arguments-length-parse-manifest.txt --count --whole, where the manifest contains one path: /workspace/adamic/stage1/typescript/parser/parser.ts. Runs alternated main/revision five times; stdout and stderr went to separate log files. All exited zero and printed 10523. Here --count is the parser's AST-node-count mode, not a counted native runtime build.

The two release binaries have SHA256 89b0b797dba305cc6b040be47a3c5d7ebe283398687189b72f60a45f867b6785. The C files also compare byte for byte. Observation: the artifacts are identical. Inference: this unit adds no generated instructions to this no-reader parser. Wall-time minima alone are not a hardware instructions/cycles measurement.

Hardware events were probed directly with perf_event_open, PERF_TYPE_HARDWARE, PERF_COUNT_HW_INSTRUCTIONS / PERF_COUNT_HW_CPU_CYCLES, exclude_kernel=1 and exclude_hv=1. Both returned errno 2, No such file or directory. /sys/bus/event_source/devices exposes breakpoint, msr and software, but no cpu PMU; perf_event_paranoid is 2. Installing a perf executable cannot supply a missing PMU. The attempted package installation also lacked sudo/root permissions. Instructions and cycles are unmeasured, not zero.
